## P02 — Azure Configuration, Secrets & Entra App Registration <a id="phase-azure-configuration"></a>

Provision and wire the only permitted Azure resources (one App Configuration store with local-dev and production labels, two Key Vaults, Entra app registrations) so the API and web app boot their configuration securely in both environments with refresh, feature flags and a local fallback.

Id `azure-configuration` · Milestone: M1 Platform foundations · Edition: Community · Status: done · Depends on: `foundation`

- [x] **P02.1** Idempotent Azure provisioning scripts (`azure-configuration-idempotent-azure-provisioning-scripts`) — done 2026-09-20 <a id="azure-configuration-idempotent-azure-provisioning-scripts"></a>
  Add infra/azure scripts (bash plus PowerShell, az CLI) that create the resource group, one App Configuration store with a sentinel key and labels local-dev/production, Key Vaults for local-dev and production with RBAC authorization and purge protection, and role assignments (App Configuration Data Reader, Key Vault Secrets User, Key Vault Crypto User) for developers and the production service principal, re-runnable with a dry-run flag, a parameter file, printed endpoints and docs/azure/bootstrap.md.
  - bash scripts/azure/provision.sh --dry-run exits 0 without creating or changing any Azure resource: it prints the az deployment group what-if result and every data-plane command it would run.
  - Running bash scripts/azure/provision.sh twice with the same parameter file leaves the second what-if with no Create or Delete entries and no Modify beyond the server-filled properties listed as what-if noise in docs/operations/azure-bootstrap.md, keeps the sentinel values, key versions and rotation policies unchanged, and both runs exit 0 with the store endpoint and vault URIs printed (verified by the owner-consented run recorded in the pull request).
  - bash scripts/azure/verify.sh confirms the store has local authentication disabled, both vaults use RBAC with purge protection, Erp:Sentinel exists under the labels local-dev and production, Erp--Platform--DataProtection--Key exists in both vaults, and every row of the documented role matrix (operator, optional developers group with Secrets User and Crypto User on the development vault, optional runtime service principal) is assigned.
  - bash scripts/azure/check.sh (bicep build with linter errors plus bash syntax checks) passes and runs in node scripts/verify/verify.ts and in the ci-backend workflow.
  - docs/operations/azure-bootstrap.md documents parameters, script order, access model and recovery; ADR-0010 is accepted and indexed; docs/configuration.md registers the sentinel key and the data-protection key.

## P03 — Backend Platform Kernel <a id="phase-backend-platform"></a>

Build the compact shared kernel that user management and every later module plug into before any business feature is written: module contract, persistence conventions and domain primitives, application primitives, HTTP/OpenAPI conventions, transport security, rate limiting and health, observability, migration tooling, and the attachments building block; background jobs and the outbox are deferred to `business-building-blocks` to keep the path to first deployment short.

Id `backend-platform` · Milestone: M1 Platform foundations · Edition: Community · Status: done · Depends on: `azure-configuration`

Platform problem writers use TryWriteAsync, so a caller that accepts no JSON keeps the status. The web rewrite proxy waits 660 s (experimental.proxyTimeout), above the 10-minute timeout ceiling.   - The health endpoints are exempt from rate limiting and from HTTP request metrics; /healthz/live answers 200 without touching any dependency; /healthz/ready runs every readiness check under a 2-second timeout and answers 503 service.unavailable, naming no check, within that bound when SQL Server is unreachable; an App Configuration store that cannot be reached after startup degrades readiness instead of failing it.
  - No output caching middleware is used: a GET endpoint marked with WithReferenceDataCaching answers a successful response with Cache-Control: private, max-age=<seconds> while every other response keeps no-store; HybridCache is registered for every host from Erp:Platform:Caching and a test proves that concurrent callers of one key share a single factory execution.
  - docs/architecture/request-pipeline.md places the rate limiter after routing, request timeouts and database cancellation and records that authentication runs before it; integration tests prove it runs after forwarded headers and before the feature gate; the web app's server-side API calls forward the browser's address (the last X-Forwarded-For entry) so production partitions per visitor; ADR-0019 is accepted and the new configuration keys are seeded so both labels resolve them.

## P05 — Authentication (Microsoft Entra ID, BFF) <a id="phase-authentication"></a>

Implement cookie-based sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID with the API as confidential OIDC client so tokens never reach the browser, plus data protection, antiforgery, bearer scheme for non-browser clients, test authentication, the login page and the authenticated app shell.

Id `authentication` · Milestone: M2 Sign-in works · Edition: Community · Status: done · Depends on: `backend-platform`, `web-foundation`

- [x] **P05.1** OIDC BFF in the API (`authentication-oidc-bff-in-the-api`) — done 2026-09-30 <a id="authentication-oidc-bff-in-the-api"></a>
  Configure Microsoft.Identity.Web AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApp from the AzureAd section (auth code + PKCE, single tenant, explicit default and challenge schemes), /api/auth/login with validated relative-only returnUrl, /api/auth/logout and callback paths, hardened cookie options (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, sliding expiry), a fallback RequireAuthenticatedUser policy with an explicit AllowAnonymous allow-list, 401 ProblemDetails instead of redirects for XHR requests, and integration tests using a TestAuthHandler scheme.
  - An anonymous request to any API route outside the anonymous allow-list, including a path no route matches, answers 401 application/problem+json with code request.unauthenticated and no Location header; a signed-in request reaches the route; a request a policy refuses answers 403 request.forbidden; an architecture test fails on any anonymous route that is on neither the permanent list (health, /api/auth/login, the Development-only OpenAPI routes) nor the transitional list of platform routes that stay open until `authentication-web-login-page-and-session-integration`
  - GET /api/auth/login?returnUrl=<local path> answers 302 to the tenant authorize endpoint with response_type=code, an S256 PKCE challenge, response_mode=form_post and redirect_uri = Erp:Platform:Identity:WebOrigin + /api/auth/signin-oidc; an absolute, protocol-relative, backslash, tilde, control-character or over-long returnUrl answers 400 request.invalid with errors.returnUrl and sets no cookie; a signed-in caller is redirected straight to the return path
  - The session cookie __Host-erp-session is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, path / and has no Expires; it slides within Erp:Platform:Identity:SessionIdleTimeout (30 minutes) and is refused after that idle time or after Erp:Platform:Identity:SessionLifetime (12 hours) from sign-in; POST /api/auth/logout clears it and redirects to the Entra end-session endpoint; a failed or cancelled callback lands on /login?error=sign-in-failed, where the page says sign-in did not finish
  - The API redeems the authorization code with the Key Vault certificate Erp:Platform:Identity:ClientCertificate through Microsoft.Identity.Web with no client secret anywhere, refuses to start when the tenant id, client id, web origin or certificate is missing or invalid, rate-limits a signed-in person as that person, and opens a download link only for the person who created it
  - Every existing Playwright spec passes without an Entra round trip, and a manual sign-in with a real Entra account against the local-dev registration completes and lands on the return path, recorded in the pull request

  - The route decides the sign-in before the rate limiter, so a bearer route limits each application or person its tokens name and ignores the session cookie, which neither signs it in nor slides there, and the antiforgery check applies exactly to the POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE requests the session cookie signs in.

- [x] **P05.8** Login hardening (`authentication-login-hardening`) — done 2026-10-10 <a id="authentication-login-hardening"></a>
  Apply strict rate limiting to auth endpoints, record sign-in/sign-out/failure events in an audit table, verify security headers and cookie flags with a Playwright test, and write docs/security/auth-threat-model.md covering CSRF, session fixation, open redirects and token leakage.
  - The sign-in paths (`/api/auth/login`, the OpenID Connect callbacks `/api/auth/signin-oidc` and `/api/auth/signout-callback-oidc`, the front-channel `/api/auth/signout-oidc` and `POST /api/auth/logout`) are limited per client address by a strict limit that runs before authentication, `Erp:Platform:RateLimiting:SignInPermitLimit` within `SignInWindow`, and a request over it answers 429 `rate-limit.exceeded` with `Retry-After`.

  - Records older than `Erp:Platform:Auditing:SecurityEventRetention` (one year, owner decision of 2026-10-10; CERT-In direction (iv) of 28.04.2022 requires a rolling 180 days within India) are deleted by a daily sweep, proven against SQL Server.

  - `docs/security/auth-threat-model.md` covers CSRF, session fixation, open redirects, token leakage, token replay and id-token misuse, the front-channel sign-out (the Entra session id is no secret), the returnUrl rules of `proxy.ts` and the sign-in page and the CSP `form-action` source of the Microsoft end-session path; the local-dev sign-in registration lists no API-origin redirect URI and the new settings are seeded in App Configuration, each after a matching preview.
  - Edition: Community (confirmed 2026-09-29)

## P06 — User Management & Authorisation <a id="phase-user-management"></a>

Manage employees as ERP users (contractors are vendors), their profiles, departments, designations, roles and permissions with a full audit trail, forming the first business module, the hand-built reference for the `business-building-blocks-module-and-feature-scaffolders` scaffolder and the gate for the first deployment.

Id `user-management` · Milestone: M3 First on-prem deployment · Edition: Community · Status: ⏳ in progress · Depends on: `authentication`

- [x] **P06.1** Users module and just-in-time provisioning (`user-management-users-module-and-just-in-time`) — done 2026-10-10 <a id="user-management-users-module-and-just-in-time"></a>
  Create backend/Modules/Identity/Users with a User aggregate linked to the Entra object id (employee code, display name, work email, phone, designation, date of joining, status) in schema `identity`, create or update the user from Entra claims on first sign-in, deny sign-in for deactivated users, bootstrap the first administrator from configuration, and add admin CRUD endpoints with validation plus unit and integration tests.
  - A person's first sign-in, through Entra or the test persona sign-in, creates an active record in identity_users.Users linked to their Entra object id with the name and work email of their claims; each later sign-in refreshes both and stamps the sign-in time, and a record an administrator registered beforehand with the same object id, or with the same work email and no object id, is linked instead of a second one being created.
  - A deactivated person's sign-in is refused with a redirect to /login?error=account-deactivated and a SignInRefused security event, and from the next request on every open session or bearer token of a person whose record is deactivated or deleted is refused with 401; reactivation lets the person sign in again, and a deleted person's next sign-in creates a new record.
  - Holders of the Erp.Admin app role can list (paged, sorted, filtered), read, register, update (employee code, phone, designation, date of joining; refused with 409 when the version is stale), deactivate, reactivate and delete people under /api/identity/users; everyone else is refused with 403, an administrator cannot deactivate or delete their own record, every invalid input answers ProblemDetails, and the OpenAPI document and the Kiota client carry the routes.
  - The sign-in page explains a refused sign-in of a deactivated account, and unit, integration, architecture and Playwright tests cover the record, the admission at sign-in and on every request, and the endpoints.
  - Edition: Community (confirmed 2026-10-10)
  - Note: Identity/Users exists (ADR-0039): identity_users.Users holds one record per person (the Entra object id, the name and work email every sign-in takes from Entra, the employee code, an E.164 phone number, a free-text designation, the date of joining, active or deactivated, the last sign-in; soft-deletable, versioned, audited). IPersonAdmission (BuildingBlocks.Application/Actors, implemented by UserAdmission) admits a person at every sign-in, creating the record or linking one registered beforehand by object id or by the work email of an unlinked record, refuses a deactivated one with /login?error=account-deactivated and the security event SignInRefused, and is checked again on every session request and every bearer token of a person, so deactivating or deleting a record ends the sessions of that person at their next request. /api/identity/users (list, get, register, update and status change with the record version, soft delete) requires the app role Erp.Admin until permissions exist, and an administrator cannot change the status of or delete their own record. EfUnitOfWork also answers a save that a unique index refuses with concurrency.conflict. The flag Erp.Modules.Identity.Users is enabled under both labels in infra/appconfig/feature-flags.json. Against the scope, the schema is identity_users (naming rule) and no administrator is bootstrapped from configuration, because the app role assignment makes one (owner decision of 2026-10-10).
- [x] **P06.2** Directory invitation via Microsoft Graph (`user-management-directory-invitation-via-microsoft-graph`) — done 2026-10-10 <a id="user-management-directory-invitation-via-microsoft-graph"></a>
  Add an invitation flow that searches directory users through Microsoft Graph, pre-registers invitees with an intended role, matches them by object id or email on first login, and covers the flow with integration tests using a fake Graph client.
  - Holders of the Erp.Admin app role search the company directory through GET /api/identity/users/directory?search= (2 to 100 characters): the API asks Microsoft Graph on behalf of the signed-in administrator with the delegated permission User.ReadBasic.All, answers at most 25 people ordered by display name with their Entra object id, display name, user principal name and mail, names the record of each one the ERP already holds (by Entra object id, or by the work email of a record linked to no Entra account) and says whether more people matched; everyone else is refused with 403.
  - POST /api/identity/users/invitations, with an idempotency key, pre-registers a directory person by Entra object id with the display name and user principal name Microsoft Graph returns and the administered details, and answers 201 with the record; an object id the directory does not hold answers 404 directory.person-not-found, an object id or employee code another record holds, or a work email that a record linked to no Entra account holds, answers 409, and the first sign-in of the person links the invited record by its object id. POST /api/identity/users registers by work email only.
  - A directory that refuses the administrator (consent missing, a sign-in interaction required, Microsoft Graph answering 401 or 403) answers 403 directory.access-denied, and one that cannot be reached or keeps throttling answers 503 directory.unavailable through the new ErrorKind.Unavailable; neither the search text nor a token reaches a log or a span.
  - entra.sh adds User.ReadBasic.All with consent for the whole organisation to both sign-in registrations and verify.sh --entra checks it; integration tests drive the search and the invitation through the real token acquisition against TestTokenEndpoint and a fake Microsoft Graph (TestDirectory) that every test host uses, and the OpenAPI document and the Kiota client carry both routes.
  - Edition: Community (confirmed 2026-10-10)
  - Note: The company directory in Microsoft Entra can be searched and invited from (ADR-0040): IPeopleDirectory (BuildingBlocks.Application/Actors) is implemented by GraphPeopleDirectory (BuildingBlocks.Authentication/Graph), a typed client of Microsoft Graph whose token is the signed-in administrator's own for the delegated User.ReadBasic.All, which entra.sh grants for the whole organisation on both sign-in registrations; GET /api/identity/users/directory?search= answers at most 25 people by display name with the record the ERP holds for each, POST /api/identity/users/invitations creates a record linked to the person's Entra account with the display name and user principal name of the directory, and POST /api/identity/users registers by work email only. A refused token or a Graph refusal answers 403 directory.access-denied and an unreachable directory 503 directory.unavailable (the new ErrorKind.Unavailable); the tests run the real token acquisition through the refresh tokens of TestTokenEndpoint and answer Graph with TestDirectory. Against the scope, an invitation gives no role: access stays an app role assigned in Microsoft Entra, and the role of an invitation arrives with user-management-roles-and-permissions (owner decision of 2026-10-10).

## P07 — First On-Prem Deployment <a id="phase-first-deployment"></a>

Take API, web app, migrator and reverse proxy live on the Ubuntu home server with Docker Compose, TLS, secrets, health gating, backups and a repeatable, attestation-verified deployment pipeline; closes M3 with user management as the only business module.

Id `first-deployment` · Milestone: M3 First on-prem deployment · Edition: Community · Status: planned · Depends on: `user-management`

- [ ] **P07.1** Production compose stack (`first-deployment-production-compose-stack`) <a id="first-deployment-production-compose-stack"></a>
  Complete infra/compose/compose.yaml and compose.production.yaml with proxy, api, web and one-shot migrator services, named volumes (data-protection keys, attachments, proxy certificates), hardened settings (read_only with tmpfs, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, resource limits, log rotation, restart unless-stopped, healthcheck on every service, depends_on service_healthy), file-backed secrets for the service-principal certificate, profiles so SQL Server never starts in production, and `docker compose config` validation in CI.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
  - Note: From backend-platform-transport-security-middleware: the API is called under three host names in production - the public host name (the edge proxy routes /api/* straight to api:8080 and passes the browser's Host through), api (the web container's server-side calls to http://api:8080) and 127.0.0.1 (the container health probe) - so the production value of Erp:Platform:Host:AllowedHosts is <public host name>;api;127.0.0.1, and Erp:Platform:Host:KnownNetworks must list the compose network so forwarded client addresses are trusted; an empty list trusts no proxy. Never set ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED. From backend-platform-attachments-building-block (ADR-0022): attachments live in Azure Blob Storage, so the stack needs no attachments volume; the production api reads Erp:Platform:Attachments:BlobServiceUri and the EncryptionKey reference from the production label that first-deployment-production-attachments-storage creates, and the edge proxy must pass /api/platform/attachments uploads of up to MaxSizeBytes plus 64 KiB and allow transfers of up to Erp:Platform:Attachments:TransferTimeout. From `authentication-token-cache-and-data-protection-key` (ADR-0032): compose.production.yaml mounts the external volume erp-ai-pro-data-protection-keys on the api at /home/app/.local/share/ERP-AI-Pro/DataProtection-Keys, so the deploy script creates it once with docker volume create erp-ai-pro-data-protection-keys before the first up and never removes it (an external volume survives docker compose down -v); the api keeps its tmpfs /tmp under read_only, because every new Data Protection key is staged there; the production label must hold Erp:Platform:DataProtection:KeyIdentifier (provision.sh writes it) and the runtime service principal must hold Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User on the production vault, or the api refuses to start.
- [ ] **P07.2** Production database provisioning (`first-deployment-production-database-provisioning`) <a id="first-deployment-production-database-provisioning"></a>
  Provision Azure SQL (serverless free offer or small provisioned tier, recorded as an ADR) with an Entra admin, contained users for the app (data role) and migrator (schema role), service-principal connection strings stored in Key Vault, firewall rules for the home server, the free-amount-remaining alert, and a documented fallback to a SQL Server Express container.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
  - Note: From backend-platform-migration-tooling-and-seeding (ADR-0021): create the migrator service principal (certificate file erp-migrator-client.pem, id in MIGRATOR_AZURE_CLIENT_ID) with App Configuration Data Reader and Key Vault Secrets User on the production store and vault, its contained database user with the schema role, the secret Erp--Platform--Database--MigratorConnectionString in kv-erp-ai-pro-prod and its production-label reference Erp:Platform:Database:MigratorConnectionString; compose.production.yaml already runs the migrator service with that identity. From `authentication-login-hardening` (ADR-0038): direction (iv) of the CERT-In Directions of 28.04.2022 under section 70B(6) of the IT Act requires the logs of every ICT system, audit.SecurityEvents included, to be kept securely for a rolling 180 days within Indian jurisdiction, so the production database and its backups stay in an Azure region in India; Erp:Platform:Auditing:SecurityEventRetention keeps the security events one year.
- [ ] **P07.3** Production attachments storage (`first-deployment-production-attachments-storage`) <a id="first-deployment-production-attachments-storage"></a>
  Provision the production storage account for attachments with the existing storage-account Bicep module (Entra only, private attachments container, blob and container soft delete, CanNotDelete lock) after asking the owner for its redundancy (locally redundant, zone-redundant across three Central India zones, or geo-redundant) and its soft-delete retention; grant Storage Blob Data Contributor on the container to the runtime service principal only; create Erp--Platform--Attachments--EncryptionKey in kv-erp-ai-pro-prod with its own value; write Erp:Platform:Attachments:BlobServiceUri and the EncryptionKey reference under the production label; optionally restrict the account to the server's fixed address; extend verify.sh to production; and prove a production upload and download round trip.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
- [ ] **P07.4** Host bootstrap runbook and scripts (`first-deployment-host-bootstrap-runbook-and-scripts`) <a id="first-deployment-host-bootstrap-runbook-and-scripts"></a>
  Write docs/runbooks/host-setup.md and infra/compose/host scripts for Ubuntu hardening (unattended upgrades, ufw, fail2ban, SSH keys only), Docker Engine install, non-root deploy user, mounted service-principal certificate, .env for non-secret values, DNS and router port-forwarding, and a systemd unit running `docker compose up -d --wait`.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
- [ ] **P07.5** Reverse proxy and TLS (`first-deployment-reverse-proxy-and-tls`) <a id="first-deployment-reverse-proxy-and-tls"></a>
  Configure the edge proxy (Caddy with automatic TLS as default, nginx+certbot as alternative, recorded as an ADR) routing /api/* to api:8080 and everything else to web:3000, TLS 1.2+, HSTS ramp-up, forwarded headers with KnownIPNetworks equal to the compose subnet, security headers, request size limits, streaming buffering off and no host-published ports other than 80/443, verified by a local end-to-end run through the proxy including the Entra redirect flow.

Adding the proxy to the local compose stack also ends the local limit: an upload over 10 MB through the web container's own /api rewrite gets no answer. From user-management-directory-invitation-via-microsoft-graph (ADR-0040): the access log of the proxy records no query string, because GET /api/identity/users/directory?search= carries a search text that names people and GET /api/platform/attachments/{id}/content?link= carries a download token; the API itself never logs either (docs/guides/observability.md).
- [ ] **P07.6** Release and deploy pipeline (`first-deployment-release-and-deploy-pipeline`) <a id="first-deployment-release-and-deploy-pipeline"></a>
  Add a release workflow on v* tags building and pushing images with SBOM, provenance, attestations and the CVE gate, and host-side deploy.sh and rollback.sh that pull by digest, run `gh attestation verify`, execute the migrator, roll api/web with health-gated cutover, prune, and roll back to the previous digest on failure, with a shellcheck CI job.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
  - Note: From backend-platform-migration-tooling-and-seeding (ADR-0021): the migrator ships inside the api image at /app/migrator as the compose migrator service (pull_policy never, restart no). docker compose up recreates a changed api container before it evaluates the api depends_on condition service_completed_successfully, so deploy.sh must pull api and web, run docker compose run --rm migrator on its own, stop and keep the running api when it exits non-zero, and only then run up -d --remove-orphans --wait. Migrator exit codes: 0 succeeded, 1 failed or cancelled, 2 configuration could not be loaded or is invalid, 3 migrations pending (status), 64 usage. docs/operations/runbooks/migrations.md is the manual form of this sequence. From `foundation-editions-and-licensing` (ADR-0030): publishing the Community images conveys LGPL-3.0-only object code, so both images carry COPYING, COPYING.LESSER and a third-party notices file (including the LGPL-3.0-or-later libvips binaries that sharp brings into the web image, with where their source is), the OCI labels org.opencontainers.image.licenses=LGPL-3.0-only, org.opencontainers.image.source, org.opencontainers.image.revision and org.opencontainers.image.vendor=Dewiride Technologies Private Limited, and each release names its tagged commit as the corresponding source. No published image may contain Microsoft.Identity.Client.NativeInterop (libmsalruntime.so, brought in by Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Extensions.Azure through Microsoft.Identity.Client.Broker), because section 3(e) of its Microsoft Software License Terms forbids distributing it: exclude its native runtime from the published hosts, or the dependency that brings it, and prove the image holds no such file. The private Enterprise images get their own labels and notices in `business-building-blocks-enterprise-edition-composition`.
- [ ] **P07.7** Health probes and uptime monitoring (`first-deployment-health-probes-and-uptime-monitoring`) <a id="first-deployment-health-probes-and-uptime-monitoring"></a>
  Provide a shell-less health probe for the chiseled API image (tiny .NET probe entrypoint or proxy-side active checks), a /api/health route in the web app, compose healthcheck definitions and an external uptime monitor hitting /healthz/live through the proxy with alerting to the owner.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
- [ ] **P07.8** Backups and restore drill (`first-deployment-backups-and-restore-drill`) <a id="first-deployment-backups-and-restore-drill"></a>
  Verify Azure SQL automated backups and PITR retention, back up the data-protection key volume, attachments volume and compose configuration nightly to an encrypted off-host location, and rehearse a full restore documented in docs/runbooks/restore.md with measured RTO/RPO.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
  - Note: From backend-platform-attachments-building-block (ADR-0022): attachments live in Azure Blob Storage, not on a volume, so their backup is the account's redundancy plus blob and container soft delete (versioning or point-in-time restore only if the owner chooses the extra cost), and the drill restores a deleted blob and a deleted container; the attachments encryption key in Key Vault (soft delete and purge protection) is as critical as the data, because losing it makes every attachment it wrapped unreadable. From `authentication-token-cache-and-data-protection-key` (ADR-0032): the volume erp-ai-pro-data-protection-keys holds the Data Protection key ring, key-<guid>.xml files wrapped by the production vault key Erp--Platform--DataProtection--Key; back it up with a separate digest-pinned helper container that has tar (the chiseled api image has no shell), restore it with the stack stopped and before the api starts, keep every Key Vault key version that wrapped a backed-up key enabled, and rehearse the loss case too: losing the volume signs everyone out and loses nothing else, and the token cache table platform_caching.DistributedCacheEntries needs no restore of its own.
- [ ] **P07.9** Go-live checklist and production smoke (`first-deployment-go-live-checklist-and-production-smoke`) <a id="first-deployment-go-live-checklist-and-production-smoke"></a>
  Run a production Playwright smoke project (real Entra test user via stored auth state, users list renders, sign-out) against the live URL, confirm traces and logs arrive, complete docs/runbooks/go-live-checklist.md, record ADR deployment topology, and mark milestone M3 done in the roadmap.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
  - Note: From backend-platform-attachments-building-block: the owner deferred the attachment virus scanner on 2026-09-26 (uploads record notScanned); decide before go-live between Microsoft Defender for Storage malware scanning (about 935 INR per storage account per month plus about 14 INR per GB scanned, asynchronous, and only possible if the stored bytes are not encrypted by the API) and a scanner on the server behind IAttachmentScanner (needs the owner's approval of a non-Microsoft package or image). From authentication-web-login-page-and-session-integration (ADR-0036): once ERP_AZURE_PRODUCTION_WEB_ORIGIN is set, run entra.sh so the production sign-in registration gets the front-channel logout URL <web origin>/api/auth/signout-oidc, then verify single sign-out with a real account (sign out of another app of the tenant, such as Outlook on the web, and the ERP session in that browser ends while one on another device stays), note which issuer form the front-channel request carries (the API accepts the v2.0 and the sts.windows.net forms of the tenant), and check that signing out of the ERP asks no account question and that its redirect to the end-session endpoint passes the web app's form-action. From `authentication-login-hardening` (ADR-0038): add to the checklist that every ICT system log (api, web, edge proxy, database) is kept securely for a rolling 180 days within Indian jurisdiction (CERT-In Directions of 28.04.2022, direction (iv)); that the office reaches the ERP within Erp:Platform:RateLimiting:SignInPermitLimit (60 requests per address per minute on each sign-in path, which people behind one public address share, so raise it in App Configuration for a larger office); and that the ERP host shares its registrable domain with no host the company does not control, because the __Secure- correlation and nonce cookies, unlike the __Host- session cookie, can be planted by such a host served over https (docs/security/auth-threat-model.md, residual risks 3, 4 and 6).

## P22 — Documents & Records Management <a id="phase-documents"></a>

Extend the attachments building block into full records management: collections, versions, permissions, retention, generated documents, search/OCR, templates and e-signature; closes M9.

Id `documents` · Milestone: M9 Operations backbone · Edition: Mixed · Status: planned · Depends on: `backend-platform`

- [ ] **P22.1** Document model and permissions (`documents-document-model-and-permissions`) <a id="documents-document-model-and-permissions"></a>
  Extend `backend-platform-attachments-building-block` into backend/BuildingBlocks/Documents with collections per module entity, versions, tags, ownership, permission inheritance from the linked entity, access audit, legal hold and retention policies enforced by a job, migrating existing attachment metadata in place, with tests.
  - Edition: Enterprise (recommended)
  - Depends on: `business-building-blocks-enterprise-edition-composition`
  - Note: From backend-platform-attachments-building-block (ADR-0022): build on BuildingBlocks.Attachments and IAttachmentService. Deleting an attachment only soft-deletes its row and keeps its content, and identical uploads share one StoredContent, so the retention job must purge a blob and its StoredContents row only when no attachment row references it any more, must honour DPDP erasure requests, and must re-wrap envelopes before a retired encryption key is removed (files.StoredContents.KeyId lists the content each key still protects); files.DownloadRedemptions is the read record until the audit-trail building block exists.
- [ ] **P22.2** Generated documents service (`documents-generated-documents-service`) <a id="documents-generated-documents-service"></a>
  Consolidate PDF generation (invoices, credit notes, payslips, Form 16, purchase orders, letters) on a shared template engine with branding, QR codes, watermarks and a digital-signature (DSC) integration point, with snapshot tests and migration of `finance-sales-invoice-pdf-rendering` and `finance-payroll-statutory-outputs-salary-tds-and-registers` renderers.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
  - Note: Edition split (ADR-0030): this item offers the template engine and migrates `finance-sales-invoice-pdf-rendering` onto it; the payslip and Form 16 renderers belong to the Enterprise payroll items, which adopt the engine in the private repository.
- [ ] **P22.3** Search and OCR (`documents-search-and-ocr`) <a id="documents-search-and-ocr"></a>
  Index metadata and extracted text with SQL Server full-text search, run OCR through `ai-platform-document-intelligence-pipeline` for scanned uploads and support saved searches, with tests.
  - Edition: Enterprise (recommended)
  - Depends on: `business-building-blocks-enterprise-edition-composition`
- [ ] **P22.4** Web: document explorer (`documents-web-document-explorer`) <a id="documents-web-document-explorer"></a>
  Build a document explorer, entity document tabs across modules, drag-and-drop upload with progress, PDF/image previewer and version history, covered by Playwright on desktop and mobile with screenshots.
  - Edition: Enterprise (recommended)
  - Depends on: `business-building-blocks-enterprise-edition-composition`
- [ ] **P22.5** Templates and e-signature (`documents-templates-and-e-signature`) <a id="documents-templates-and-e-signature"></a>
  Add a template library (NDA, offer letter, contractor agreement) with merge fields and an e-signature request adapter interface storing signed documents.
  - Edition: Enterprise (recommended)
  - Depends on: `business-building-blocks-enterprise-edition-composition`
- [ ] **P22.6** AI: document intelligence (`documents-ai-document-intelligence`) <a id="documents-ai-document-intelligence"></a>
  Add Documents/Ai for auto-tagging and classification, contract clause and renewal-date extraction and semantic search.
  - Edition: Enterprise (recommended)
  - Depends on: `business-building-blocks-enterprise-edition-composition`
  - Tags: ai

## P28 — Integrations Platform & Public API <a id="phase-integrations"></a>

Connect the ERP to the outside world with a connector framework, public API and webhooks, Microsoft 365, engineering-tool, government/tax and banking connectors and an import/export centre; closes M12.

Id `integrations` · Milestone: M12 Insight and connectivity · Edition: Mixed · Status: planned · Depends on: `backend-platform`

- [ ] **P28.1** Integration framework (`integrations-integration-framework`) <a id="integrations-integration-framework"></a>
  Create backend/BuildingBlocks/Integrations with a connector abstraction (auth, sync jobs, mapping, error handling, replay), per-connection secrets in Key Vault, connection health, rate-limit awareness and idempotency, with a fake connector under test.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
- [ ] **P28.2** Public API and webhooks (`integrations-public-api-and-webhooks`) <a id="integrations-public-api-and-webhooks"></a>
  Expose a versioned public API secured by `authentication-session-endpoints-openapi-security-and-bearer` bearer tokens or API keys with scopes, hashing and rotation, outbound webhook subscriptions with HMAC signatures and retries, per-client rate limits and a developer documentation page, with integration tests.
  - Edition: Community (recommended)
  - Note: From `authentication-session-endpoints-openapi-security-and-bearer` (ADR-0034): the bearer scheme exists but no route takes it. Give the registration an Application ID URI (api://<client id>), the public API's delegated scopes and its application-only app roles, whose values never equal Erp.User or Erp.Admin, and the idtyp access-token optional claim with include_user_token, through scripts/azure/lib/graph.sh and verify.sh; protect the route group with RequireBearerToken(new BearerTokenAccess(scopes, applicationRoles)) and switch Erp.Platform.Identity.BearerTokens on per label; an API key scheme added beside it needs its own policy scheme choice in RouteSignInScheme, because a route names one scheme only. From `authentication-login-hardening` (ADR-0038): a refused bearer token is validated and recorded as a security event inside authentication, ahead of the global rate limiter, so a client sending refused tokens costs a signature check and an insert into audit.SecurityEvents each, without limit; bound that before the first route takes bearer tokens (a per-address limit on bearer requests ahead of authentication, or a cap on the refusals recorded per address and window), and add that route to the API header check of frontend/e2e/tests/smoke/web-security.spec.ts.
- [ ] **P28.3** Microsoft 365 connectors (`integrations-microsoft-365-connectors`) <a id="integrations-microsoft-365-connectors"></a>
  Integrate Graph calendar (interviews, leave), SharePoint/OneDrive document sync and Teams notifications with contract tests against recorded responses.
  - Edition: Enterprise (recommended)
  - Depends on: `business-building-blocks-enterprise-edition-composition`
- [ ] **P28.4** Engineering tool connectors (`integrations-engineering-tool-connectors`) <a id="integrations-engineering-tool-connectors"></a>
  Integrate GitHub, Azure DevOps and Jira for timesheet hints and project task sync, with contract tests.
  - Edition: Enterprise (recommended)
  - Depends on: `business-building-blocks-enterprise-edition-composition`
- [ ] **P28.5** GST and identity connectors (`integrations-gst-and-identity-connectors`) <a id="integrations-gst-and-identity-connectors"></a>
  Implement adapter interfaces and sandbox tests for GST/GSP APIs (GSTR-2B download, live e-invoice IRP over `finance-sales-e-invoicing-adapter`) and PAN/GSTIN verification, each behind feature flags.
  - Edition: Enterprise (recommended)
  - Depends on: `business-building-blocks-enterprise-edition-composition`
- [ ] **P28.6** Direct-tax and labour connectors (`integrations-direct-tax-and-labour-connectors`) <a id="integrations-direct-tax-and-labour-connectors"></a>

## P29 — Operations: Observability, DR, Security Hardening & Privacy <a id="phase-operations-hardening"></a>
